final_answer: Apparent change in frequency due to relative motion between source and observer.

A sound source, moving at a constant speed of $240\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ towards a detector, emits sound at a constant frequency. The detector records a frequency of $5\text{ }100\text{ Hz}$.

Take the speed of sound in air as $340\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$.
question: Calculate the wavelength of the sound emitted by the source.
memo:
$f_L = \frac{v \pm v_L}{v \pm v_s} f_s$
$5\text{ }100 = \frac{340 + 0}{340 - 240} f_s$ $\checkmark$
$f_s = 1\text{ }500\text{ Hz}$ $\checkmark$
$v = f\lambda$ $\checkmark$
$340 = (1\text{ }500)\lambda$ $\checkmark$
$\lambda = 0,23\text{ m}$ $\checkmark$

passage: A particle, P, with a charge of $+5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}$, is located $1,0\text{ m}$ along a straight line from particle V, with a charge of $+7 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}$. A third charged particle, Q, at a point $x$ metres away from P, experiences a net electrostatic force of zero newton.
question: Calculate the distance $x$.
memo:
$$\frac{k Q_P Q}{(x)^2} = \frac{k Q_V Q}{(1 - x)^2} \checkmark$$
$$\frac{(9 \times 10^9)(5 \times 10^{-6})Q}{x^2} = \frac{(9 \times 10^9)(7 \times 10^{-6})Q}{(1 - x)^2} \checkmark$$
$$6,708(1 - x) = 7,937x \checkmark$$
$$x = 0,458\text{ m} \checkmark$$
$$x = 0,46\text{ m} \text{ (away from P)} \checkmark$$
